# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 77 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 77 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_077_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 7

**1** After a few days I saw him in the same plain where I had also seen the shepherds; and he said to me, "What do you seek?" **2** I said to him, "Lord, that you would command the shepherd who punishes to depart from my house; for he afflicts me greatly." **3** "It is necessary for you to be afflicted," he said, "for thus the glorious angel commanded concerning you, for he wishes you to be tested." **4** "Why? What evil thing have I done, that I should be handed over to this angel?" I asked. **5** "Listen," he said; "your sins are many, yet not so many that you should be handed over to this angel; but your household has committed great iniquities and sins, and the glorious angel has been embittered against them on account of their deeds, and therefore he commanded that you should be afflicted for a time, in order that they also might repent and be cleansed from all worldly desire. **6** When therefore they repent and are cleansed, then the angel of punishment shall depart." **7** I said to him, "Lord, if they have done such things that the glorious angel has been embittered, what have I done?" He answered, "They cannot be afflicted otherwise, unless you, the head of the household, are afflicted; for when you are afflicted, of necessity they also are afflicted; but when you are well-off, they can have no affliction." **8** I said to him, "But behold, Lord, they have repented with their whole heart." **9** "I know," he said, "that they have repented with their whole heart. Do you think that the sins of those who repent are forgiven immediately? Not at all — but the one who repents must torture his own soul, and he must be greatly humbled in all his conduct and be afflicted with many kinds of affliction; and if he endures the afflictions that come upon him, certainly he who created all things and endued them with power will be moved to compassion and will provide some remedy. **10** And this will be, if he sees the heart of every penitent pure from every evil thing. And it is profitable for you and your household to be afflicted now. But why do I speak much? You must be afflicted as the angel of the Lord commanded, he who delivered you to me. And give thanks for this to the Lord, that he deemed you worthy to show you beforehand the affliction, that knowing it beforehand you might be able to bear it with strength."

---

*EMET renders affliction (thlipsis) with strict lexical precision throughout. The "glorious angel" (angelos endoxos) is distinguished from the angel of punishment (angelos tes timorías).*
